notes: frozen before any experiment; every experiment is compared against it

notes: max_chunks from EDA token counts: p99 of windows per text is 8 for English and 4 for German

change: one model per language with its own feature/regularisation search (cased words and char n-grams offered to German)
notes: motivated by EN/DE differences in EDA: German capitalises nouns, compounds words and has only two domains

change: two-stage: stage-1 domain classifier routes each text to a per-domain expert (same features and model as B0)
notes: domains have very different class priors and styles; domains below min_domain_docs fall back to the global model

change: two-stage with routing by the given domain column instead of the stage-1 prediction
notes: domains have very different class priors and styles; domains below min_domain_docs fall back to the global model

change: open-weight LM likelihood features (observer/performer log-probs, entropy, Binoculars ratio, spread over 64-token segments) + gradient boosting

change: two-stage stacked ensemble: stage 1 diverse base models (word/char TF-IDF, per-language, per-domain, label cascade, encoder, LM features); stage 2 per-language gradient-boosting stacker over their scores, the given domain, encoder window stats, LM and text-statistic features
notes: stacker is trained and scored with group k-fold inside the validation split (out-of-fold predictions), then refit on all validation rows for test

change: X4 plus per-language class offsets added to the stacker log-probabilities, tuned for macro-F1 by grid search
notes: offsets for each validation fold are tuned on the other folds' out-of-fold predictions, so the validation score stays out-of-sample; test uses offsets tuned on all validation rows

change: two-stage label cascade: stage 1 ai vs not-ai, stage 2 human-vs-fusion specialist trained only on human and fusion texts (B0 features and model)
notes: replaces domain routing as the two-stage idea (domain is given in test); B0's human/fusion boundaries also have to separate ai texts, the specialist only separates the hard pair

change: character n-grams (char_wb 3-5, cased, first 2000 characters) instead of word n-grams, small C search
notes: added as a diverse ensemble member: splits text differently from the word models; trained on a 120k subsample (11.2 GB peak, about 2 min; macro-F1 0.763 at 20k, 0.792 at 60k, 0.808 at 120k)
